items.claim: The span is one formula-bounded unit under this book's own frame: a strict-form word-event onset stands at MT 35:1, the witness records a pe after MT 34:31 behind it, the set-your-face direction opener follows at MT 35:2 with the behold-I-am-against-you verdict device at MT 35:3, and the strict recognition refrain at MT 35:15 with a pe after it closes both unit and chapter. The three interior recognition clauses at MT 35:4, MT 35:9 and MT 35:12 are each followed by continuation rather than by an onset device, so none of them is row-final, and the addressee stays Mount Seir across all fifteen verses.
items.both_sides: Front seam MT 34:31 / MT 35:1: the close side carries the last shepherd-oracle verse with a pe after it, the onset side a word-event whose bytes are identical to the one at MT 36:16. Rear seam MT 35:15 / MT 36:1: the close side carries the strict recognition refrain plus a pe, the onset side the and-you-son-of-man sub-onset that pivots the same word-event frame to the mountains of Israel. Interior: the samekh after MT 35:13 is disclosed and correctly does not cut, because the messenger formula at MT 35:14 keeps the same addressee and no refrain stands between them; the two causal paragraphs at MT 35:5 and MT 35:10 follow the closes at MT 35:4 and MT 35:9 without any onset device, which is why those closes are paragraph-final and not row-final. Whole-chapter span held at the ruled ceiling for such spans, with the cap disclosed. Flag answer: the out-of-span verses this row argues (MT 6:7, 28:22, 30:8, 37:6, 37:13 and 39:6 as comparanda for interior recognition closes, and MT 33:1, 33:23, 34:1, 36:16, 37:15 and 38:1 as the onset series) are context and move no seam, while both of this row's own seam verses are carried in its evidence list, so the unmirrored-reference flag is not a defect here.

items.both_sides: Front seam MT 35:15 / MT 36:1: strict recognition refrain plus pe on the close side, sub-onset on the onset side, with the shared word-event frame disclosed on both rows rather than claimed twice. Rear seam MT 36:12 / MT 36:13: the close side carries the recognition-family refrain at MT 36:11 and a samekh after MT 36:12 with no onset device between them; the onset side carries a messenger formula together with a real addressee change, since the address runs 2mp and then 2ms to the end of MT 36:12 and is unambiguously 2fs from MT 36:13 onward. Interior: the samekh after MT 36:4 falls mid-chain and is disclosed as non-cutting, which the bytes support, because the addressee never changes and each link of the chain opens with a consequence particle rather than a fresh address. Flag answer: the unmirrored references are the wider two-sided-unit range named as context; both of this row's own seam verses are in its evidence list, so the flag is not a defect. The unit-type move to a restoration classification is disclosed with a byte ground, that the addressee is Israel's own territory and not a foreign nation, which the operative-category rule permits.

items.claim: The boundary prose calls MT 36:16 the fourth and last word-event hard seam since MT 33:1 and enumerates only MT 33:1, MT 33:23 and MT 34:1. The strict-form word-event onsets from MT 33:1 onward are MT 33:1, MT 33:23, MT 34:1, MT 35:1 and MT 36:16, so MT 36:16 is the fifth, MT 35:1 is missing from the enumeration, and two further such onsets follow at MT 37:15 and MT 38:1. The count is wrong in both directions, and the neighbouring row in this same stretch correctly counts MT 35:1 as the fourth.
items.both_sides: The boundary itself is untouched by the miscount and its high confidence stands. Front seam MT 36:15 / MT 36:16: the close side carries a doubled utterance formula at MT 36:14 and MT 36:15 with a samekh after MT 36:15; the onset side carries the strongest onset class in the book, a strict word-event byte-identical to MT 35:1, with the son-of-man address and a change of tense and topic at MT 36:17. Rear seam MT 36:23 / MT 36:24: the close side carries the utterance formula plus a recognition clause in the nations' mouth, a ruled close, so the refrain does close the unit before the seam; the weakness at that seam is on the onset side, which belongs to the following row, not to this close. Interior: the samekh after MT 36:21 is disclosed and correctly not cut, because MT 36:22 opens a consequence clause inside the same profaned-name argument rather than a new addressee. Flag answer: the single-curly-quoted formula name in the prose is a delimiter matter and not a form error; the wording it names is the recognition-family clause of MT 36:23 addressed to the nations, and it is used as texture, not to move a boundary.

items.claim: The onset device the row names at MT 36:24, a causal conjunction set in the delimiters this corpus reserves for translation wording, is not in the Hebrew of that verse: MT 36:24 opens with a waw-consecutive perfect and carries no causal particle at all. The onset side of this row therefore holds no onset device of any tier-1 class and no paragraph mark, the whole warrant for the seam is the utterance-formula close on the far side at MT 36:23, and that verse is argued in the prose without being carried in the evidence list. One-sided seam evidence does not support a high confidence.
items.both_sides: Close side of the onset seam: MT 36:23 carries the utterance formula plus a recognition clause addressed to the nations, a ruled close and genuinely refrain-grade, but no parashah mark; the nearest recorded mark is the samekh after MT 36:21, which falls a verse and a half earlier, so the Masoretic paragraphing breaks before this seam rather than at it. Onset side: MT 36:24 carries no word-event, no messenger formula, no addressee change, no hand or transport verb and no mark; what it does carry is the gather-and-return promise, which is a unit-type device rather than a boundary onset, and the conjunction the prose leans on is supplied by the translation. Rear seam MT 36:32 / MT 36:33 is sound in contrast: utterance formula with a samekh after MT 36:32 on the close side, messenger formula on the onset side. One sound seam and one one-sided seam reads medium. Flag answer: most of the unmirrored list is the neighbouring span named as context, but MT 36:23 inside it carries this row's entire onset warrant, which is why the gap matters here rather than elsewhere. Byte check on the retained citation-form hazard: this row's two contrasted Hebrew strings, MT 36:26 and MT 11:19, are both whole-verse matches to the witness extract, so no de-accented citation form reached the row.

items.claim: The boundary prose treats the emphatic I-Yahweh-have-spoken close at MT 36:36 and the samekh recorded on that verse as internal and not final because a second messenger re-onset follows at MT 36:37. That inverts the ruled reading of the device: a fresh onset standing after a mid-unit close is precisely the condition that makes that close row-final, and a messenger formula immediately behind a refrain-grade close is a licensed cut. The reason as written argues for the cut the row declines to make.
items.both_sides: Onset seam MT 36:32 / MT 36:33: utterance formula with a samekh after MT 36:32 on the close side, messenger formula on the onset side, licensed exactly because a refrain close stands immediately before it. Interior MT 36:36 / MT 36:37: the close side carries the emphatic close plus a samekh, the onset side a second messenger formula, so the cutting condition is met there as well; what defeats the cut is size, not the presence of that second onset, because MT 36:37 to MT 36:38 would be two verses and is not a word-event unit. The row states that size ground in its rejected-alternative field, so its outcome is right and only the stated reason is reversed. Rear seam MT 36:38 / MT 37:1: strict recognition refrain with a samekh after MT 36:38 on the close side, a hand-of-Yahweh vision onset on the onset side. Flag answer: MT 36:32 is argued as the close behind this row's onset without being carried in its evidence list, the same small gap that appears twice elsewhere in this cluster; MT 33:21, MT 33:22 and MT 37:1 are context and move no seam.

suggested_fix.fact: the ground for keeping MT 36:37 to MT 36:38 inside this row is the under-three-verse floor and the absence of a word-event onset there, not the presence of the messenger formula at MT 36:37; a following onset is what would make the emphatic close at MT 36:36 row-final

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The book's planning text states the size of the messenger chain at MT 36:2-36:7 twice and the two statements disagree, once as six and once as seven. The witness bytes read six occurrences on six verses and the formula census agrees, and the row followed the six.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: A later lane that takes the seven will look for a seventh occurrence that the bytes cannot source, and may argue an interior cut in that chain from a digit rather than from a device.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the seam at MT 36:23/36:24 should exist at all, rather than merely carry a lower confidence. On the ruled reading a mid-unit utterance formula is paragraph-final unless a fresh onset follows, and no onset follows at MT 36:24; the alternative shape is one row over MT 36:16-36:32 with a cap disclosure.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: This lane ordered a confidence move rather than a merge, because a seventeen-verse row would sit outside the ruled density band and the close at MT 36:23 is genuinely refrain-grade. The choice between the two remedies is a real fork and a second opinion on it is worth having.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: At MT 35:14 and MT 35:15 the pronominal object addressed to Mount Seir is written in the form that elsewhere marks a feminine singular addressee, while MT 35:3-35:12 addresses it as masculine singular. The ordinary pausal reading is masculine, and this lane treats it as such.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It qualifies nothing in this cluster's boundaries, but the neighbouring cut at MT 36:12/36:13 is argued from an addressee-gender change, so a lane that later reads MT 35:14-15 as feminine should know that the cut at MT 36:13 rests on a whole cluster of feminine forms across three verses and not on a single pronoun.
